subject: Bridgeline: week-ahead priorities, active blockers, and decision requests
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Matt Chen <matt.chen@nova-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Bridgeline: week-ahead priorities, active blockers, and decision requests

Team —

Quick week-ahead check-in ahead of the QBR prep calls. Keeping this tight so execs can skim and action. Attached: ops heatmap (page 1 = latency/cost trends by route), and a one-pager for QBR narrative.

Wins:
- Completed rollout of prefix caching for search-heavy customers; Nova Analytics recorded a 27% token-cost drop in staging.
- Instrumented per-route cold-start metrics in Console; we now surface 95th p99 for every model route.
- Canary of new batching kernel in us-west shows 1.2x throughput with <10ms added tail latency.

Risks / open items:
1) Nova Analytics acceptance test failing on S3-proxied payloads (error 504) — CS flagged. Needs infra trace and quick config fix; impact: one renewal at risk.
2) Dedicated pool autoscaler regression after kernel change — observed oscillations when burst traffic drops below threshold. Risk to latency SLO on high-throughput tenants.
3) QBR narrative gap: we lack a crisp economics slide showing unit cost reduction (tokens/$) by optimization trio (caching, batching, quantization).

Asks (what I need this week):
- Markus: can your infra team prioritize the S3-proxy trace for Nova? If we can triage within 24h, CS can proceed with their acceptance window.
- Maya: please pull a short chart (1 slide) showing token unit economics before/after prefix caching + batching for the top 5 routes; drop into the Drive link.
- Laura: request an exec slot to call out customer risk if we can't close Nova's acceptance by Thursday.

Proposed mitigation steps:
- Short-term: revert S3-proxy config to prior timeout for Nova while we root-cause.
- Medium-term: put a guard in autoscaler to avoid <10s oscillation thresholds.

Attachments: 2027-04-19_ops-heatmap.pdf (summary), qbr-prep-one-pager.docx

Thanks,
Jonas
---
Jonas Weber
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Matt Chen <matt.chen@nova-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Bridgeline: week-ahead priorities, active blockers, and decision requests

Jonas —

Thanks for the concise summary. Quick responses below and a couple of asks of my own.

On Nova S3 proxy (1):
- I'll assign Priya from infra to run a full trace; initial thought is the signed-url refresh policy plus a proxy connection-timing edge case. We can try the revert but want a trace before toggling in-prod.
- ETA for trace: 6 hours; will update channel and CS.

On autoscaler oscillation (2):
- Agree we need a guard. I'll scope a conservative debounce fix and aim for a canary in staging Wed morning. If safe, roll to canary tenants Thu.

On unit economics slide (3):
- Ops/measurements look good; Maya will own the chart but I need the raw route IDs and cost map to validate.

Asks from infra:
- Jonas, can you confirm which high-throughput tenants we treat as canary for the debounce fix? Prefer a mix of hosted + dedicated.
- Laura, if we escalate a temporary SLA exception for one tenant while we stabilize autoscaler, do we route approvals through you or finance?

Also tagging Matt (Nova): if reverting the proxy timeout is problematic on your side, let us know — we can coordinate a short maintenance window tonight.

-Markus

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Bridgeline: week-ahead priorities, active blockers, and decision requests

Jonas / Markus —

I'll take the economics slide. Plan: pull top 5 routes by request volume (last 30d), compute tokens-per-request and $/k tokens pre/post prefix-caching and with the new batching kernel. Deliverable: single-slide PNG + data CSV in Drive by EOD Wed (2027-04-21).

On Nova acceptance: I can validate the cost win numbers in staging, but I need the exact customer route IDs and the CS acceptance test steps — Matt, can you paste the failure steps here or in the Drive ticket?

On canary selection for autoscaler: recommend we use a hosted tenant (alpha-svc) and one dedicated pool (dp-east-1-small) as Markus suggested. That gives a good traffic mix.

I'll also add a short note to the QBR one-pager explaining the mitigation timeline and the impact if unpatched.

Thanks,
Maya

Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Bridgeline: week-ahead priorities, active blockers, and decision requests

Folks —

Thanks for the updates. Jonas, please escalate Nova with the CS timeline; if acceptance is at risk by Thursday, I'll join the call and offer a short exec commitment (we can propose a 2-week grace and a punitive SLA credit if necessary).

On the autoscaler guardrail: prioritize stability over micro-optimizations for QBR. Markus, if the canary looks safe, prepare a single-slide ask for the exec meeting that proposes the guard + timeline + customer impact estimate.

Maya: appreciate the slide runbook; drop it in the Drive link and flag any gaps.

I'll block a 20-min slot on Thu afternoon for a rapid sync (exec + infra + CS) once Markus and Priya have the trace.

Laura
